resources.string: clipsync uses this service only to notice when the clipboard changes, because Android blocks background clipboard access for normal apps. It reads the clipboard content when you copy — nothing else. It does not read your screen, log keystrokes, or collect analytics. Clipboard data goes only to your own paired devices, end-to-end encrypted. Nothing is sent to any server.
Why clipsync needs the accessibility permission

Android 10+ blocks apps from reading the clipboard in the background. The accessibility service is the only reliable way for clipsync to capture what you copy, system-wide.

What it reads: the clipboard, when its content changes. Nothing else.
What it never does: read screen content, log keystrokes, collect analytics.
Where your data goes: only to your own paired devices, end-to-end encrypted. There is no server.
